author: human
request:
Bug report: opening /owners?page=0 — or any page value below 1 — renders the
error page instead of the owner list. Expected behavior: the owner listing
treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal
listing (HTTP 200). Find the cause, fix it, and cover the fix with a test.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Owner listing treats a page below one as the first page
summary: Opening the owner listing with a page value below 1 (0 or negative) shows the error page today. The listing must treat any such value as the first page and respond with the normal listing.
acceptance_criteria: given more than one owner matching the search, when the owner listing is requested with page=0, then it responds HTTP 200 with the normal owner listing showing the first page, identical to a page=1 request

given more than one owner matching the search, when the owner listing is requested with a negative page value (e.g. page=-1), then it responds HTTP 200 with the normal owner listing showing the first page
a request with page=1 or higher behaves exactly as before
non_goals: non-numeric page values: behavior unchanged, not decided by the owner
page values beyond the last page: behavior unchanged, not decided by the owner
the error page's exposure of exception detail (REQ-SYS-002 known defect) stays a separate slice
any change to search matching or to the single-match redirect (REQ-OWN-002)
notes: Intake line 1 carries no decisions array entries; scope rests on the quoted request alone. No Non-Goals row touched, so no scope_overrides. The owner quoted the HTTP 200 status in the request; the PRD states it behaviorally. One data-driven test covers page=0 and a negative value. Autofix audit: no prd-autofix records on the log.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Covered by the OwnerController Contracts row (system-design.md § Contracts, 'search with paging') and the Web controller row of architecture-principles.md § DDD building blocks, which states that normalizing a request parameter to its permitted range is binding, not a business rule. The fix is a clamp inside OwnerController. Cause (grep of the source, weaker basis without the IDE oracle): processFindForm passes the raw page into findPaginatedForOwnersLastName, which calls PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize). PageRequest.of rejects a negative page index with IllegalArgumentException, and the error page renders it. The fix clamps page to a minimum of 1 once, at the top of processFindForm, before both the repository query and addPaginationModel. That way currentPage in the model is 1, and page=0 and page=-1 render exactly as page=1 does, as the first acceptance criterion requires. Keep the clamp in the handler and leave OwnerRepository and the domain unchanged. Per testing-principles.md, a rule the design assigns to the web controller is tested at the web level through MockMvc, not extracted for a unit test. The only design write is REQ-OWN-005 joining the OwnerController Contracts row.
integration_points: Repository boundary (OwnerRepository) double: reuse the existing @MockitoBean OwnerRepository stub in OwnerControllerTests, the one framework-stub exception testing-principles.md § Mocking Policy tolerates. Reason: the class is a @WebMvcTest slice with no JPA context, so a real implementation is unavailable. A hand-written double of the whole JpaRepository-derived interface costs more setup than the assertion. Stub findByLastNameStartingWith with a Page of two or more owners. Capture or match the Pageable argument to assert it is page index 0, and assert model attribute currentPage == 1.
Framework transport: MockMvc, the sanctioned web test harness (CLAUDE.md § Testing Strategy).

Binding: no new entry point. GET /owners keeps binding page as an int request parameter and Owner as the search form, with the existing disallowed-fields binder; the change is normalizing that bound value (security-principles.md § Mass assignment unaffected).

patterns.description: existing search-text normalization (null to empty, strip) in processFindForm; the page clamp belongs alongside it as the same kind of request-parameter normalization

risks.risk: Clamping only inside findPaginatedForOwnersLastName leaves currentPage at 0 or a negative value in the model, so the pagination links render differently from page=1 and break 'identical to a page=1 request'
risks.mitigation: Normalize the page once at the top of processFindForm and pass the normalized value to both helpers (architecture-principles.md § Web controller: binding normalizes the request)

risks.risk: Scope creep into non-numeric or beyond-last-page values, or into VetController
risks.mitigation: prd-entry non_goals exclude both; leave the int binding and the upper bound unchanged

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records on the log; skipped. Observation for product-requirements-expert, not in this slice's scope: VetController.findPaginated uses the same PageRequest.of(page - 1, ...) shape, so /vets.html?page=0 very likely fails the same way (REQ-VET-001). It is neither fixed nor recorded as a Known Defect here, pending a product decision.

blast_radius.note: One production line of logic plus a constant in OwnerController.processFindForm, one new controller test, and two doc lines registering REQ-OWN-005; single module, no sensitive or security-surface paths.

semantic_surprise.note: Read the hunk: Math.max(page, 1) runs once at the top of the handler before both PageRequest.of(page - 1, 5) and the currentPage model attribute, so page 0 and negatives behave exactly like page 1 and every page of 1 or higher is untouched; no guard removed, no boundary flipped, and Integer.MIN_VALUE clamps safely.

test_adequacy.note: The parameterized MockMvc test drives page=0 and page=-1 and asserts HTTP 200, the listing view, currentPage=1 and the exact owner list; without the clamp PageRequest.of throws on a negative index, so the test would fail on the unfixed code, and the existing page=1 test still covers the unchanged path.
